description: The >>TURN { exception-name [file-name]... }... { CHECKING ON [WITH LOCATION] | CHECKING OFF } compiler directive (ISO §2023:7.3.25) - it enables and disables exception checking for the source text that follows. Recognized and parsed by TurnDirectiveProcessor into the TurnEvent list the checking model reads; the introduction gate rejects the directive word below 2002 through the ONE ConstructRegistry funnel - it emitted a bespoke COBOL0875 until kb/Work PB725, which RETIRED that code (never reallocate). THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): COBOL-85 has no compiler directives, its only compiler-directing forms being statements (§1985:IV.6.4.2.2.1: 'The compiler directing verbs are COPY, ENTER, REPLACE, and USE'), so a '>>' line cannot occur in a conforming COBOL-85 source; ISO/IEC 1989:2002 introduces the directive (§2002:7.2.2 SR5: 'A compiler directive is composed of the compiler directive indicator') and §2002:F.2 lists the facility as a change, its item 29: 'Compiler directives instruct the compiler to take specific actions during compilation'. The directive is in the 2002 text: §2002:7.2.19.3 GR1: 'The default TURN directive is >>TURN EC-ALL CHECKING OFF'; and §2002:F.2 names it, its item 28: 'This is enabled by the TURN compiler directive and changes to the USE statement'. 2014 keeps it (§2014:7.3.20: 'The TURN directive is used to turn checking for specified exception conditions on or off') and so does 2023 (§2023:7.3.25.1).

directiveOperand.citation: ISO §2023:7.3.25.2 general format + §2023:7.3.25.3 SR1/SR3/SR4: an exception-name list with optional file-names and a CHECKING phrase — a structured operand, diagnosed by its own stage as COBOL0718/COBOL0719.

source:
>>TURN EC-ALL CHECKING ON
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. PB725TU.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
           DISPLAY "X".
           STOP RUN.
